clues: This town lies in a wide valley in the west of Colorado. A big river runs past its south edge, with high cliffs north.
Hot summers and cold winters clash here in a sharp split. Yet the sun warms winter days well above freezing.
The Ute people lived here first, and farmers came with founder William Pabor in 1884. Ten years on, the town was made official.
The big river past town once had a grander name. In old days, that same river was called the Grand River.
The Book Cliffs are the sight that gives this town away. That long range of cliffs marks the north edge of the whole valley.
